subproblem.title: Bounded open Lipschitz piece carrying the part of a C¹ antilipschitz chart over a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ), let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, let c > 0 satisfy c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, and let K ⊆ ℝ^Q be compact (ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with the Euclidean norm). Then there exist an open set s ⊆ ℝⁿ and a constant L ∈ ℝ≥0 such that s ⊆ Ω, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s, s is bounded, and Φ is L-Lipschitz on s.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (K : Set (Eucl Q)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → IsCompact K → ∃ (s : Set (Eucl n)) (L : ℝ≥0), IsOpen s ∧ s ⊆ Ω ∧ Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' K ⊆ s ∧ Bornology.IsBounded s ∧ LipschitzOnWith L Φ s
subproblem.natural_proof:
Setting and notation.
- Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, c > 0 satisfies c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, and K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with the Euclidean norm |·|; B_r(x) is the open ball and B̄_r(x) the closed ball.
- This is steps 2–3 of the parent proof: the choice of the bounded open set s = Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀) and the Lipschitz bound on it, applied there with K = tsupport h.

1. (Empty case.) Suppose Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅. Take s := ∅ and L := 0. Then:
   - s is open, s ⊆ Ω, and s is bounded;
   - Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅ ⊆ s;
   - every map is 0-Lipschitz on ∅ (Mathlib `lipschitzOnWith_empty`).
   This proves the claim in this case. From now on assume Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ≠ ∅.

2. (Choice of the ball.) Fix w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ K. K is compact, hence bounded, so there is D ∈ ℝ with |y − y′| ≤ D for all y, y′ ∈ K (`Metric.isBounded_iff`). Put ρ := D/c + 1 and s := Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀).

3. (s is open, contained in Ω, and bounded.) s is the intersection of the open sets Ω and B_ρ(w₀), so s is open. Clearly s ⊆ Ω. Also s ⊆ B_ρ(w₀), a bounded set, so s is bounded.

4. (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s.) Let v ∈ Ω with Φ(v) ∈ K.
   - Apply the lower bound to w = v, w′ = w₀ (both in Ω), then the choice of D (Φ(v), Φ(w₀) ∈ K): c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ D.
   - Dividing by c > 0 gives |v − w₀| ≤ D/c < D/c + 1 = ρ, so v ∈ B_ρ(w₀).
   - Together with v ∈ Ω this gives v ∈ s.

5. (Bound on the derivative.) Since Φ is C¹, the map x ↦ DΦ(x) = fderiv ℝ Φ x is continuous (`ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`, using 1 ≤ 1). The closed ball B̄ := B̄_ρ(w₀) is compact (finite dimension). So there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖DΦ(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ B̄ (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`). Put L := max(C, 0) = Real.toNNReal C ∈ ℝ≥0. Then ‖DΦ(x)‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ B̄.

6. (Mean value inequality.) Φ is differentiable at every point (C¹, 1 ≠ 0) and B̄ is convex. The mean value inequality on convex sets (`Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le`, with ‖DΦ(x)‖₊ ≤ L on B̄) gives |Φ(x) − Φ(x′)| ≤ L|x − x′| for all x, x′ ∈ B̄. That is, Φ is L-Lipschitz on B̄.

7. (Restriction to s.) s ⊆ B_ρ(w₀) ⊆ B̄, so Φ is L-Lipschitz on s (`LipschitzOnWith.mono`).

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 3, 4 and 7, the set s and the constant L satisfy all the requirements: s is open, s ⊆ Ω, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s, s is bounded, and Φ is L-Lipschitz on s. ∎

Lean note: every lemma used is in the frozen scope `import GMT.Ch06.Submission`. The proof is a single theorem with no imports and no helpers.
proof_key_steps: If Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅, take s = ∅ and L = 0 (lipschitzOnWith_empty).
Otherwise pick w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ K and a distance bound D for K; set ρ = D/c + 1 and s = Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀). Then s is open, s ⊆ Ω, and s is bounded.
Antilipschitz bound: c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ D gives |v − w₀| < ρ, hence Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s.
DΦ is continuous, so ‖DΦ‖ ≤ C on the compact convex ball B̄_ρ(w₀). The mean value inequality makes Φ (Real.toNNReal C)-Lipschitz on B̄_ρ(w₀) ⊇ s.

audit.reason: The prose and exact one-line proposition agree on all hypotheses and conclusions. The proof handles the empty case, constructs the bounded open piece using the positive lower Lipschitz bound, and bounds the derivative on a compact convex ball. Global C¹ regularity justifies using that ball even outside Ω. The mean value inequality and restriction prove the required Lipschitz conclusion. No parent or sibling theorem is assumed.
